AAPL.rationale: Apple presents a solid but not compelling fundamental picture. The company delivered strong YoY growth in Q2 FY2026 (revenue +16.6%, EPS +21.8%), with gross margins expanding to 49.3% and operating margins of 32.4%. Services revenue hit $30.98B, supported by a 2.5B device installed base, providing a high-margin recurring revenue stream. The balance sheet is healthy with total equity of $106.5B and debt-to-equity of 0.78, while operating cash flow of $28.7B in the quarter and a $100B buyback authorization signal strong capital return. However, the QoQ trajectory is weak (revenue -22.7%, EPS -29.2%) reflecting normal seasonality after the holiday quarter, and the TTM picture is incomplete due to fiscal calendar gaps. Valuation is elevated: P/E of 37.4x sits in the upper half of its 30-43x 12-month range, P/B of 43x is rich, and the 2.7% earnings yield is modest. The stock has already rallied 19.6% in the past quarter and 50%+ over the past year, pricing in much of the positive narrative. The near-term catalyst is WWDC (June 8-12), where a rebuilt AI-powered Siri and Apple Intelligence updates could re-rate the stock if execution matches expectations—Morgan Stanley sees potential to $440. However, this is partially priced in given the recent run, and UBS remains skeptical on Apple's broader AI strategy. Regulatory headwinds (EU DMA €500M fine, Supreme Court App Store ruling, DOJ antitrust) and China competitive pressure from Huawei represent real risks. The leadership transition to John Ternus adds execution uncertainty. Overall, Apple is a high-quality franchise with durable competitive advantages, but at current valuation with the stock near all-time highs, the risk-reward is only mildly attractive.
